name: rowQuantiles
title: Estimates quantiles for each row in a matrix

origin.description: Estimates quantiles for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
rowQuantiles(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, probs = seq(from = 0, to = 1,
  by = 0.25), na.rm = FALSE, type = 7L, digits = 7L, ...,
  useNames = TRUE, drop = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An integer, numeric, or logical N by K matrix with N >= 0.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: probs
arguments.text: A numeric vector of J probabilities in [0, 1].

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: An integer specifying the type of estimator. See stats::quantile.

arguments.name: digits
arguments.text: An integer specifying the precision of the formatted percentages. Not used when useNames is FALSE.
Additional arguments passed to stats::quantile. fuzz is the one used by quantile.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: If TRUE, singleton dimensions in the result are dropped, otherwise not.

origin.details: When the matrix has no missing values and type is 7, each row is sorted with sort.int(partial=) and the quantile is interpolated without clamping probs. Any missing value, or another type, calls stats::quantile on that row. A row with a missing value is NA when na.rm is FALSE. Percentage names such as 25% and 75% come from the internal formatter.
origin.value: An N by J matrix, where N is the number of selected rows and J is the number of probabilities. A single row or a single probability drops to a vector when drop is TRUE. Type 7 returns double. Another type returns the storage mode of x when no row is calculated, and double when stats::quantile runs.

translation.description: Estimates quantiles for each row in a matrix.
translation.usage:
rowQuantiles(x, rows=None, cols=None, probs=None, na_rm=False, type=7,
  digits=7, use_names=True, drop=True, fuzz=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An N by K array. Axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. Integer, floating, and logical arrays are accepted. A vector is rejected.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based rows to include. None uses every row. Zero is dropped, a negative value excludes, and a missing subscript inserts a missing row.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based columns to include. None uses every column.

arguments.name: probs
arguments.text: Probabilities. None is 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1. Values may sit within 100 * machine epsilon of [0, 1].

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, missing values are dropped before the quantile. A double missing value is nan. An integer missing value is -2147483648.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Quantile type 1 through 9. The default 7 matches stats::quantile. Type 7 with no missing values does not clamp probs.

arguments.name: digits
arguments.text: Precision of the percentage names. Ignored when use_names is false. A fractional value is truncated toward zero.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: If true, the result carries percentage names such as 25% and 75% on .colnames, or on .names after a row drops to a vector.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: If true, a result with one row or one probability becomes a one-dimensional array.

arguments.name: fuzz
arguments.text: Passed to the stats::quantile path. None uses R's default, which is 0 for type 7 and 4 * machine epsilon otherwise. The type-7 path with no missing values ignores it.

translation.details: A full sort selects the same order statistics as sort.int(partial=). Type 7 with no missing values interpolates 1 + (n - 1) * probs and errors if a partial index is outside 1:n. Other cases follow R 4.5 stats::quantile, including floor(nppm * (1 + fuzz)) for types other than 7. Percentage names are built inside this function.
translation.value: An array of shape (selected rows, probabilities). Double results are float64. An untouched integer allocation, when type is not 7 and a margin is empty, is int32 filled with -2147483648. .colnames holds the percentage names.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowquantiles import rowQuantiles

rowQuantiles(np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F"), probs=[0.25, 0.75])
